issues.t: Cranks but won't start (fuel pump main relay)
issues.sym: The engine turns over but won't fire, often when the car is hot or after it has sat in the sun. It may start again once it cools down. You may not hear the fuel pump hum when you turn the key.
issues.why: The main relay that powers the fuel pump and injectors develops cracked solder joints with age and heat, so it stops sending power. RepairPal has more than 80 owner reports of this no-start on the Integra.
issues.next: Have a shop check for fuel pump power while the problem is happening. A new or resoldered main relay is a cheap fix; don't let anyone replace the fuel pump until the relay has been ruled out.

issues.t: Distributor failure: stalling or no spark
issues.sym: The engine misfires, stalls while driving, or cranks without starting. It often happens on high-mileage cars and may come and go at first.
issues.why: The distributor houses the ignition coil and igniter, which wear out with heat and age. Owners report replacing the whole distributor, not just the cap and rotor.
issues.next: Have the ignition system tested for spark. Replacing the cap and rotor is cheap maintenance, but a failed coil or igniter usually means a new or remanufactured distributor.

issues.t: Oil leak at the distributor and check engine light
issues.sym: Oil on the back of the cylinder head below the distributor, and sometimes a check engine light or rough running if oil gets inside the distributor.
issues.why: The O-ring that seals the distributor to the cylinder head hardens with age and lets oil seep out, and the shaft seal can let oil into the distributor itself. RepairPal lists this for 1990-2001 Integras at about 135,000 miles on average.
issues.next: Replace the distributor O-ring soon; it's a cheap part. If oil is inside the distributor cap, the distributor seal or the whole unit may need replacing.

issues.t: Squeal from the distributor that sounds like a loose belt
issues.sym: A loud squeal or chirp from the engine that sounds like a slipping belt, even after the belts are adjusted or replaced.
issues.why: On high-mileage cars the bearing inside the distributor wears out and squeals. RepairPal notes it is often mistaken for a belt problem.
issues.next: Ask a shop to confirm where the noise comes from with a stethoscope before replacing belts. A worn distributor bearing usually means replacing the distributor.

issues.t: Rough, high or hunting idle
issues.sym: The idle speed surges up and down, stays too high when warm, or the engine idles roughly.
issues.why: The fast idle thermo valve and the idle air control valve get dirty or loose with age, so the engine computer can't hold a steady idle.
issues.next: Have the throttle body, fast idle thermo valve and idle air control valve cleaned. Replace the idle air control valve if cleaning doesn't help, and check for vacuum leaks.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the valve cover gasket and cam plug
issues.sym: Oil on top of or around the engine, a burning oil smell after driving, or oil drips on the transmission side.
issues.why: The rubber valve cover gasket and the O-ring on the plastic camshaft end plug harden with age and start to seep.
issues.next: Replace the valve cover gasket and cam plug O-ring together. Both are inexpensive and stop oil from dripping on hot exhaust parts.

issues.t: Radiator cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Green coolant under the front of the car, a sweet smell, the low coolant level, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The plastic radiator tanks become brittle with age and crack, especially on high-mileage cars. Owners report radiator failures at around 180,000 km.
issues.next: Don't drive if the engine is overheating. Replace the radiator and check the hoses and cap at the same time.

issues.t: Sunroof leaks water inside
issues.sym: Water drips from the headliner, the dome light area or down the pillars after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: The sunroof's drain tubes clog with dirt and leaves, so water overflows into the cabin instead of draining out.
issues.next: Clear the drain tubes with low air pressure or a flexible line. Dry the carpet promptly to prevent mold and electrical problems.

issues.t: Knocking from worn rear trailing arm bushings
issues.sym: A metallic knock from the rear on uneven roads, and the rear end may feel loose.
issues.why: The large rubber bushings in the rear trailing arms crack after about 10 years and eventually break.
issues.next: Have the rear bushings inspected and replaced in pairs. Check ball joints and tie rods at the same time; owners say they wear on these cars too.

issues.t: Temperature gauge reads low or stops moving
issues.sym: The temperature gauge slowly reads lower than normal, then the needle may stop moving at all, even though the engine is warm.
issues.why: The single-wire coolant temperature sender for the dashboard gauge wears out. It's separate from the sensor the engine computer uses.
issues.next: Make sure the engine actually warms up and the thermostat works. Replacing the gauge sender is inexpensive.

issues.t: Alternator stops charging
issues.sym: The battery light comes on, lights dim, or the battery keeps going dead.
issues.why: The alternator wears out with age and mileage. Owners of these cars report alternator replacements.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. Replace the alternator if output is low, and check the battery since a weak one adds strain.

issues.t: Burns some oil between changes
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, sometimes with a little blue smoke on startup.
issues.why: Owners say slight oil burning is common on high-revving Integra engines, and some RSX Type-S owners report the same. Worn rings or valve seals make it worse with age.
issues.next: Check the oil level every other fill-up and top it off. If you're adding more than about a quart every 1,000 miles, have a compression and leak-down test done.

issues.t: Water in the trunk from leaking taillight seals
issues.sym: Water pools in the trunk or spare tire well, or moisture shows inside the taillights.
issues.why: The rubber gaskets behind the taillights harden and shrink with age and let water in. Owners report it on both Integras and RSXs.
issues.next: Replace the taillight gaskets or reseal the housings. Dry out the trunk to stop rust and musty smells.

issues.t: Manual transmission grinds or pops out of 3rd gear
issues.sym: Grinding when shifting into 2nd or 3rd, especially on quick shifts, 3rd gear that is hard to get into, or the shifter popping out of 3rd. It usually starts mild and gets worse.
issues.why: The 3rd gear synchronizer or the 3-4 shift sleeve wears. Acura Service Bulletin 08-018 covers this on the 6-speed, and earlier bulletins covered gear grinding on these manuals.
issues.next: Try fresh Honda manual transmission fluid first; it sometimes helps. If grinding continues, the transmission needs a rebuild with new synchros. Shift gently to slow the wear.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold (compressor failure)
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or cycles on and off, sometimes with noise from the compressor.
issues.why: The A/C compressor or its clutch fails on many of these cars, and leaks in the system are common. Owners report this can be a costly repair.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks and pressure. A failed compressor is usually replaced along with the drier and a system flush.

issues.t: Check engine light from the VTC oil control valve
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with rough idle or less power. Codes often relate to cam timing.
issues.why: The oil control valve that runs the variable valve timing (VTC) can stick or get clogged with debris. An Acura bulletin covers VTC faults from a contaminated or stuck solenoid. RepairPal reports it at about 72,500 miles on average.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Change the oil if it's overdue, then clean or replace the VTC oil control valve and its screen.

issues.t: Check engine light from a failed EVAP purge valve
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with an evaporative emissions code. The car usually drives normally.
issues.why: The purge valve that sends fuel vapor into the engine fails. RepairPal reports it at about 94,000 miles on average.
issues.next: Check the gas cap first. If the code returns, replace the purge valve; it's not urgent but the car may fail an emissions test.

issues.t: Timing chain or tensioner rattle and cam timing codes
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine, often at startup, and a check engine light with cam or crank timing codes.
issues.why: An Acura bulletin covers timing-related codes from the timing chain, tensioner, sprocket or low oil pressure. The tensioner wears and lets the chain slap.
issues.next: Have the codes and oil pressure checked. Replace the tensioner, and the chain if it's stretched, before it can jump a tooth.

issues.t: Clutch master cylinder squeaks, then fails
issues.sym: The clutch pedal squeaks, then feels soft, sticks to the floor, or the car is hard to shift because the clutch doesn't fully release.
issues.why: The clutch master cylinder wears internally. Acura issued a bulletin for clutch pedal squeak, and owners report master and slave cylinder failures.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid level. Have the hydraulics bled or the master cylinder replaced; owners recommend flushing the fluid regularly.

issues.t: Power window cable snaps or window sticks
issues.sym: The window drops into the door, moves slowly or crooked, makes a grinding noise, or the auto-up stops working.
issues.why: The cables in the window regulator fray and break. Owners report a moderately expensive repair.
issues.next: Tape the window up if it falls, then replace the regulator. Clean and lubricate the window channels to reduce strain.

issues.t: Power door locks won't lock or unlock
issues.sym: One door won't lock or unlock with the switch or remote, or it makes a buzzing sound.
issues.why: The door lock actuators wear out. Acura issued a bulletin for power locks that won't work.
issues.next: Have the failing door's actuator replaced. Use the key in the meantime.

issues.t: Broken engine or transmission mount
issues.sym: Clunking when shifting or getting on and off the gas, and more vibration in the cabin at idle.
issues.why: The rubber in the engine and transmission mounts tears with age. TrueDelta owners report both failing.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected. Replacing a torn mount stops the clunk and protects the exhaust and axles.

issues.t: Check engine light from a failed oxygen sensor
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, and fuel economy may drop.
issues.why: The upstream air-fuel (oxygen) sensor is the most-reported failure on the RSX. Owners say it often fails around 80,000-100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the codes read and replace the failed sensor. Don't ignore it for long; a bad sensor can hurt the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Starter clicks or won't crank
issues.sym: You hear a click or nothing when you turn the key, even though the battery is good.
issues.why: The starter motor wears out. It's one of the most-reported RSX repairs on TrueDelta.
issues.next: Have the battery and cables tested first, then test and replace the starter.

issues.t: Exhaust leak or rattle at the header flex joint
issues.sym: A rattle or louder exhaust sound, especially on hard acceleration, and possibly an exhaust smell.
issues.why: Acura bulletins cover exhaust leaks at the flexible joint behind the exhaust header and rattling heat shields.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected. Fix leaks near the engine promptly so fumes don't get into the cabin.

issues.t: Harsh or noisy automatic downshifts when slowing
issues.sym: The automatic makes a hard or noisy shift from 3rd to 2nd or 2nd to 1st as you slow down, or the D light flashes.
issues.why: Acura issued bulletins for harsh downshifts on these automatics and set rules for replacing shift solenoids. Old fluid makes it worse.
issues.next: Change the fluid with genuine Honda ATF and have the codes read. Ask a dealer about the related bulletins and software updates.

issues.t: Seat seams split or seat covers come loose
issues.sym: Seat upholstery seams pull apart, or the seat covers come loose near the headrests.
issues.why: The seat covers are a known weak spot. The most-reported RSX complaint on CarComplaints is a seat seam coming apart, and Acura issued bulletins about loose covers at the headrests.
issues.next: Have an upholstery shop restitch it before the tear spreads, or replace the cover.

issues.t: Sticky or notchy steering (recall)
issues.sym: The steering feels sticky or notchy, takes extra effort, or doesn't return to center on the highway. Some owners notice it more in cold weather.
issues.why: The steering gearbox may have been built with too much internal friction. Recall 24V-744 covers 2023-2025 Integra and 2024-2025 Integra Type S, and Acura bulletin 24-037 describes the repair.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer will replace the worm gear spring and regrease the gearbox for free.

issues.t: Stability control unit may leak brake fluid (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal travels further than usual, or the car creeps while Brake Hold is on.
issues.why: A ball valve in the vehicle stability assist (VSA) unit can leak brake fluid. Recall 23V-430 covers the 2023 Integra.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer replaces the VSA modulator for free. Don't rely on Brake Hold until it's fixed.

issues.t: Driver seat frame may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: The driver's seat feels loose or shifts, especially under braking.
issues.why: The driver's seat cushion frame may not have been tightened properly at the factory. Recalls 24V-859 and 26V-054 cover the 2024 Integra.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer replaces the seat cushion frame for free.

issues.t: Check engine light with code P0011 (valve timing)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0011, a cam timing (VTC) fault.
issues.why: Acura Service Bulletin 24-026 says the engine computer doesn't control oil flow to the variable valve timing precisely enough, so the timing overshoots its target.
issues.next: Check the oil level and top off if low. Have a dealer apply the engine software update from bulletin 24-026.

issues.t: Door window weatherstrip comes loose
issues.sym: The rubber seal along the door window frame pulls loose or sits out of place, which can cause wind noise.
issues.why: Acura Service Bulletin B23090A covers loose door sash weatherstrips.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to reinstall or replace the weatherstrip under warranty.

issues.t: Wipers stop working after blade changes or snow
issues.sym: The windshield wipers stop moving, move out of sync, or make noise after the blades were changed or pulled away from the glass in snow.
issues.why: Acura Service Bulletin B23110A says changing the blade inserts the wrong way, or lifting the arms in snow and ice, can damage the wiper motor linkage.
issues.next: Follow the owner's manual when changing blades. If the wipers act up, have the linkage checked before driving in rain or snow.
